To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

tctex1, an important subunit of the axonal transport motor complex dynein, interacts directly and specifically with N- and/or P/Q-type voltage-gated Ca2+-channels, but not L- and/or T-type Ca2+channels.

t-complex testes-expressed 1 protein, a light chain of the dyneins motor protein complex, interacts with N- and Q-type Ca2+ channel proteins, but not L type Ca2+ channel protein, and that this interaction is essential for the surface expression of N- and Q type Ca2+ channels.
tctex1, a light chain of the dyneins, interacts with N- and PQ-type VGCCs and that this interaction is important in determining their surface expression and trafficking.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that regulate the surface expression of voltage-gated Ca2+-channels (VGCCs), and how this process is altered in neurological diseases.
the mechanisms underlying the sorting and trafficking of Ca2+ channel isoforms in neurons.
the mechanisms that underlie the sorting of neuronal voltage-gated calcium channels (Ca2+) channels with distinct functions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the interaction of tctex1 with Ca2+ channels is essential to the sorting and trafficking of N-type, P-type, and Q-type VGCCs in neurons.

the tctex-1 protein is an important factor in determining the sorting and trafficking of Ca2+ channel isoforms in neurons, and that it is a potential therapeutic target for the development of novel antiepileptic drugs.
tctex1 is an important regulator of Ca2+ channel trafficking and function in neurons, which is achieved by selective binding to and modulation of Ca2+ currents.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
tctex1 is a Ca2+ channel accessory subunit that regulates the surface expression of N- and P-type Ca2+ channel in neurons.
we have found a new mechanism to sort and traffic Ca2+ channels to the cell surface.
the t-complextex1 (tct) protein, a component of the dyneinc motor complex, is involved in sorting and trafficking of Ca2+channels with different functional characteristics in neurons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the tctex-1 protein, which is part of the cytoskeletal motor complex, is able to bind to Ca2+ channels that are important for neuronal function and is able to regulate their surface expression.
the tctex 1–Ca2 + channel interaction is important in determining sorting and surface expression of neuronal Ca2 + channels.
tctex1, a subunit of dynein, is a novel Ca2+ channel auxiliary subunit that selectively binds to N- and P-type Ca2+ channel complexes and is essential for their surface expression in neurons.
